children: Musk on AI
Walter Isaacson
profiled Musk
that was released in 2023. In a new interview with Isaacson on "The Builders," Musk shares his latest conflicted thoughts on AI.
Musk said there is a chance that AI can be negative and an existential threat to humanity.
"There’s nothing I can do to stop it," Musk said.
The billionaire said when it comes to AI he has two choices: "be a participant or be a spectator."
Musk told Isaacson that the keys to a good AI are curiosity and truth-seeking, as forcing Ai to believe two things that can’t both be true can make AI insane.
"An insane AI model is not a safe one."
On the flip side, Musk said a curious AI "will want to foster humanity."
Musk was asked by Isaacson if we are in a simulation.

The billionaire isn’t sure either way and said that he once had dinner with a physicist and computer scientist. When he asked them the question about the odds we are living in a simulation, one answered 100% and one answered zero percent.
Musk said he should answer 50% as a result.
The SpaceX CEO said sometimes he questions this very notion and wonders if the fact that he is working to send people to Mars and build out a multi-planetary society are signs of a simulation.

title: Elon Musk Says AI Could Be a Threat, but He Can’t Stop It: ‘Be Participant or be a Spectator’
